claim: Sexual selection can explain the rapid evolution of fertilization proteins.
source: Sexual selection can explain the rapid evolution of fertilization proteins, yet sperm proteins evolve rapidly even if not directly involved in fertilization.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general principle about sexual selection and protein evolution.

claim: Sperm proteins evolve rapidly even if not directly involved in fertilization.
source: Sexual selection can explain the rapid evolution of fertilization proteins, yet sperm proteins evolve rapidly even if not directly involved in fertilization.
evidence: This is a key observation stated in the abstract that motivates the study.

claim: Abalone sperm secrete enormous quantities of lysin and sp18 that are stored at nearly molar concentrations.
source: In the marine mollusk abalone, sperm secrete enormous quantities of two rapidly evolving proteins, lysin and sp18, that are stored at nearly molar concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in the manuscript.

claim: Lysin and sp18 are rapidly evolving proteins.
source: In the marine mollusk abalone, sperm secrete enormous quantities of two rapidly evolving proteins, lysin and sp18, that are stored at nearly molar concentrations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by evolutionary analysis in the manuscript.

claim: High packaging of lysin and sp18 is achieved by associating into FITZ complexes upon binding FITZAP.
source: We demonstrate that this extraordinary packaging is achieved by associating into Fuzzy Interacting Transient Zwitterion (FITZ) complexes upon binding the intrinsically disordered FITZ Anionic Partner (FITZAP).
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and demonstrated through multiple experiments.

claim: FITZAP is an intrinsically disordered protein.
source: We demonstrate that this extraordinary packaging is achieved by associating into Fuzzy Interacting Transient Zwitterion (FITZ) complexes upon binding the intrinsically disordered FITZ Anionic Partner (FITZAP).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by NMR data showing lack of regular secondary structure.

claim: FITZ complexes form at intracellular ionic strengths.
source: FITZ complexes form at intracellular ionic strengths and, upon exocytosis into seawater, lysin and sp18 are dispersed to drive fertilization.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by dynamic light scattering and NMR experiments at different salt concentrations.

claim: Upon exocytosis into seawater, lysin and sp18 are dispersed from FITZ complexes to drive fertilization.
source: FITZ complexes form at intracellular ionic strengths and, upon exocytosis into seawater, lysin and sp18 are dispersed to drive fertilization.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experiments showing reduced binding affinity at high salt concentrations.

claim: Lysin uses a common molecular interface to bind both FITZAP and its egg receptor VERL.
source: NMR analyses revealed that lysin uses a common molecular interface to bind both FITZAP and its egg receptor VERL.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by NMR chemical shift perturbation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: As sexual selection alters the lysin-VERL interface, FITZAP coevolves rapidly to maintain lysin binding.
source: As sexual selection alters the lysin-VERL interface, FITZAP coevolves rapidly to maintain lysin binding.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by species-specific binding affinity measurements.

claim: FITZAP-lysin interactions exhibit a similar species-specificity as lysin-VERL interactions.
source: FITZAP-lysin interactions exhibit a similar species-specificity as lysin-VERL interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by fluorescence polarization binding assays shown in Figure 5.

claim: Tethered molecular arms races driven by sexual selection can generally explain rapid sperm protein evolution.
source: Thus, tethered molecular arms races driven by sexual selection can generally explain rapid sperm protein evolution.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, based on the findings about FITZAP-lysin-VERL coevolution.

claim: Genes associated with fertilization are often the fastest evolving in any genome.
source: Genes associated with fertilization are often the fastest evolving in any genome (Swanson and Vacquier, 2002), and in mammals, spermatozoa-specific genes show the greatest divergence between species (Torgerson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In mammals, spermatozoa-specific genes show the greatest divergence between species.
source: Genes associated with fertilization are often the fastest evolving in any genome (Swanson and Vacquier, 2002), and in mammals, spermatozoa-specific genes show the greatest divergence between species (Torgerson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Torgerson et al., 2002.

claim: Sexual selection acting on gamete recognition proteins is postulated to create reproductive barriers and facilitate speciation.
source: Sexual selection acting on gamete recognition proteins is postulated to create reproductive barriers and facilitate speciation (Arnold and Houck, 2016; Wilburn et al., 2017), but sexual selection theory has not previously explained why sperm proteins that do not directly interact with the egg evolve rapidly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Sexual selection theory has not previously explained why sperm proteins that do not directly interact with the egg evolve rapidly.
source: Sexual selection acting on gamete recognition proteins is postulated to create reproductive barriers and facilitate speciation (Arnold and Houck, 2016; Wilburn et al., 2017), but sexual selection theory has not previously explained why sperm proteins that do not directly interact with the egg evolve rapidly.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Sexual selection can propagate through protein interaction networks and potentially drive global evolution of the sperm proteome.
source: Here, we demonstrate that sexual selection can propagate through protein interaction networks and potentially drive global evolution of the sperm proteome.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as the main finding of the study.

claim: Abalone is a classic system to study molecular barriers to hybridization.
source: The marine mollusk abalone is a classic system to study molecular barriers to hybridization (Lewis et al., 1982) and is the source of the first discovered pair of interacting reproductive proteins: sperm lysin and the egg vitelline envelope receptor of lysin (VERL) (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Lewis et al., 1982.

claim: Sperm lysin and egg VERL are the first discovered pair of interacting reproductive proteins.
source: The marine mollusk abalone is a classic system to study molecular barriers to hybridization (Lewis et al., 1982) and is the source of the first discovered pair of interacting reproductive proteins: sperm lysin and the egg vitelline envelope receptor of lysin (VERL) (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Swanson and Vacquier, 1997.

claim: Animal eggs are surrounded by an extracellular barrier called the vitelline envelope that restricts the entry of sperm.
source: Animal eggs are surrounded by an extracellular barrier called the vitelline envelope (VE) that restricts the entry of sperm (the mammalian VE is referred to as the zona pellucida, ZP).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as general biological knowledge.

claim: The mammalian vitelline envelope is referred to as the zona pellucida.
source: Animal eggs are surrounded by an extracellular barrier called the vitelline envelope (VE) that restricts the entry of sperm (the mammalian VE is referred to as the zona pellucida, ZP).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as nomenclature clarification.

claim: VERL is a major component of the abalone vitelline envelope.
source: VERL is a major component of the abalone VE which lysin dissolves by binding to repetitive domains within VERL (Raj et al., 2017; Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Lysin dissolves the vitelline envelope by binding to repetitive domains within VERL.
source: VERL is a major component of the abalone VE which lysin dissolves by binding to repetitive domains within VERL (Raj et al., 2017; Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Changes in VERL over millions of years have resulted in positive sexual selection on lysin and a coevolutionary chase to maintain binding affinity.
source: Over millions of years, changes in VERL have resulted in positive sexual selection on lysin and a coevolutionary chase to maintain binding affinity.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background on lysin-VERL coevolution.

claim: Extant lysins dissolve conspecific vitelline envelopes more efficiently than those of closely related taxa.
source: Extant lysins dissolve conspecific VEs more efficiently than those of closely related taxa, providing one mechanism of species-specific fertilization and a barrier to hybridization (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997; Vacquier and Lee, 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Species-specific lysin-VERL interactions provide one mechanism of species-specific fertilization and a barrier to hybridization.
source: Extant lysins dissolve conspecific VEs more efficiently than those of closely related taxa, providing one mechanism of species-specific fertilization and a barrier to hybridization (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997; Vacquier and Lee, 1993).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: VE dissolution is mediated by non-enzymatic lysin-VERL binding.
source: As VE dissolution is mediated by non-enzymatic lysin-VERL binding, the process is concentration dependent and sperm express enormous quantities of lysin (Lewis et al., 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: VE dissolution is concentration dependent.
source: As VE dissolution is mediated by non-enzymatic lysin-VERL binding, the process is concentration dependent and sperm express enormous quantities of lysin (Lewis et al., 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical consequence of non-enzymatic binding.

claim: Sperm express enormous quantities of lysin.
source: As VE dissolution is mediated by non-enzymatic lysin-VERL binding, the process is concentration dependent and sperm express enormous quantities of lysin (Lewis et al., 1982).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: A single male abalone can contain >1 gram of lysin, reflecting >0.1% of its total body weight.
source: A single male abalone can contain >1 gram of lysin, reflecting >0.1% of its total body weight.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a quantitative measure of lysin abundance.

claim: Lysin is stored in a specialized secretory granule termed the acrosome.
source: Lysin is stored in a specialized secretory granule termed the acrosome.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: The acrosomal concentration of lysin is estimated to be ~0.1–1.0 M based on electron microscopy.
source: Based on electron microscopy (Haino-Fukushima and Usui, 1986; Lewis et al., 1980) we estimate that the acrosomal concentration of lysin is ~0.1–1.0 M, in stark contrast to saturation concentrations of ~0.001 M under in vitro conditions (Wilburn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and based on electron microscopy data from cited sources.

claim: The saturation concentration of lysin under in vitro conditions is ~0.001 M.
source: Based on electron microscopy (Haino-Fukushima and Usui, 1986; Lewis et al., 1980) we estimate that the acrosomal concentration of lysin is ~0.1–1.0 M, in stark contrast to saturation concentrations of ~0.001 M under in vitro conditions (Wilburn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation to Wilburn et al., 2018.

claim: Sp18 is a fusogenic paralog of lysin that likely mediates plasma membrane fusion between egg and sperm.
source: Another is sp18, a fusogenic paralog of lysin that likely mediates plasma membrane fusion between egg and sperm (Swanson and Vacquier, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: The receptor of sp18 is unknown.
source: The receptor of sp18 is unknown, but given its interaction with the abalone egg, its accelerated evolution is likely due to sexual selection (Aagaard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a gap in knowledge.

claim: The accelerated evolution of sp18 is likely due to sexual selection given its interaction with the abalone egg.
source: The receptor of sp18 is unknown, but given its interaction with the abalone egg, its accelerated evolution is likely due to sexual selection (Aagaard et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference based on its egg interaction.

claim: Sp18 is nearly as abundant as lysin.
source: Sp18 is nearly as abundant as lysin, so it must also be packaged at high concentrations, yet its fusogenic properties make it even less soluble than lysin (Kresge et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background information.

claim: Sp18 must be packaged at high concentrations.
source: Sp18 is nearly as abundant as lysin, so it must also be packaged at high concentrations, yet its fusogenic properties make it even less soluble than lysin (Kresge et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical inference from its abundance.

claim: The fusogenic properties of sp18 make it even less soluble than lysin.
source: Sp18 is nearly as abundant as lysin, so it must also be packaged at high concentrations, yet its fusogenic properties make it even less soluble than lysin (Kresge et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: A new family of small acrosomal proteins termed sp6 was discovered by shotgun transcriptomics and proteomics.
source: Recently, a new family of small acrosomal proteins termed sperm protein 6 kDa (sp6) was discovered by shotgun transcriptomics and proteomics (Palmer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Sp6 is rapidly evolving and hypothesized to evolve via sexual selection.
source: While also rapidly evolving and hypothesized to evolve via sexual selection, initial efforts to identify an egg binding partner for sp6 were unsuccessful (Palmer, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Initial efforts to identify an egg binding partner for sp6 were unsuccessful.
source: While also rapidly evolving and hypothesized to evolve via sexual selection, initial efforts to identify an egg binding partner for sp6 were unsuccessful (Palmer, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citation.

claim: Lysin and sp18 are highly positively charged proteins (+12 to +24).
source: However, while lysin and sp18 are highly positively charged proteins (+12 to +24), isoforms of sp6 are highly anionic (−6 to −16) and include an N-terminal poly-aspartate region of variable length (1–11 residues).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a characterization of these proteins.

claim: Isoforms of sp6 are highly anionic (−6 to −16).
source: However, while lysin and sp18 are highly positively charged proteins (+12 to +24), isoforms of sp6 are highly anionic (−6 to −16) and include an N-terminal poly-aspartate region of variable length (1–11 residues).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a characterization of sp6.

claim: Sp6 includes an N-terminal poly-aspartate region of variable length (1–11 residues).
source: However, while lysin and sp18 are highly positively charged proteins (+12 to +24), isoforms of sp6 are highly anionic (−6 to −16) and include an N-terminal poly-aspartate region of variable length (1–11 residues).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural feature of sp6.

claim: The rapid evolution of sp6 is due to intra-sperm protein coevolution with lysin and sp18.
source: We demonstrate that the rapid evolution of sp6 is due to intra-sperm protein coevolution with lysin and sp18 to allow for their dense storage in the acrosome via novel Fuzzy Interacting Transient Zwitterion (FITZ) complexes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a main finding of the study.

claim: Heterodimers of lysin-sp6 or sp18-sp6 form through hydrophobic interactions.
source: Heterodimers of lysin-sp6 or sp18-sp6 form through hydrophobic interactions, and these heterodimers polymerize into large particles (diameter >100 nm) through ionic interactions of the complementary positive and negative charges.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by NMR and DLS data.

claim: Lysin-sp6 or sp18-sp6 heterodimers polymerize into large particles (diameter >100 nm) through ionic interactions of complementary positive and negative charges.
source: Heterodimers of lysin-sp6 or sp18-sp6 form through hydrophobic interactions, and these heterodimers polymerize into large particles (diameter >100 nm) through ionic interactions of the complementary positive and negative charges.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by dynamic light scattering data in Figure 4.

claim: Upon secretion of acrosomal contents into highly ionic seawater, FITZ complexes are disrupted.
source: Upon secretion of the acrosomal contents into highly ionic seawater, FITZ complexes are disrupted, and the dispersal of lysin and sp18 facilitating fertilization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by experiments showing salt-dependent binding.

claim: Dispersal of lysin and sp18 facilitates fertilization.
source: Upon secretion of the acrosomal contents into highly ionic seawater, FITZ complexes are disrupted, and the dispersal of lysin and sp18 facilitating fertilization.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a functional consequence of FITZ complex disruption.

claim: In red abalone, two FITZAP isoforms (FITZAP-4D and FITZAP-8D) result from alternative splicing of different versions of exon 1 with a common exon 2.
source: In red abalone (Haliotis rufescens), two isoforms (FITZAP-4D and FITZAP-8D) result from alternative splicing of different versions of exon 1 (signal peptide and the N-terminus with the poly-aspartate region) with a common exon 2 (C-terminus) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both FITZAP isoforms were smaller than their cDNA open reading frame predicted (~3–4 kDa vs ~6 kDa) as revealed by mass spectrometry.
source: Each isoform was purified using strong anion exchange (SAX) chromatography and reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC), with mass spectrometry revealing that both isoforms were smaller than their cDNA open reading frame predicted (~3–4 kDa vs ~6 kDa).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: The observed masses of FITZAP isoforms are consistent with proteolytic processing by the Golgi enzymes furin and carboxypeptidase B.
source: The observed masses are consistent with proteolytic processing of FITZAP by the Golgi enzymes furin and carboxypeptidase B (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Both lysin and sp18 co-eluted with FITZAP at high-salt concentrations by SAX chromatography despite their high net positive charges.
source: Despite their high net positive charges, both lysin and sp18 co-eluted with FITZAP at high-salt concentrations by SAX chromatography (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Sp18 (+22) eluted at higher salt concentrations than lysin (+12), which mirrors the elution profiles of FITZAP-4D (−10) and FITZAP-8D (−8), respectively, suggesting isoform-specific interactions.
source: Particularly striking is that sp18 (+22) eluted at higher salt concentrations than lysin (+12), which mirrors the elution profiles of FITZAP-4D (−10) and FITZAP-8D (−8), respectively, suggesting isoform-specific interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1, with the interpretation suggesting isoform-specific interactions.

claim: Purified lysin showed no affinity for anion exchange resin.
source: While purified lysin showed no affinity for anion exchange resin, its elution was retarded when mixed with either FITZAP-4D or FITZAP-8D in vitro, albeit less dramatically than the ex vivo samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Lysin elution was retarded when mixed with either FITZAP-4D or FITZAP-8D in vitro.
source: While purified lysin showed no affinity for anion exchange resin, its elution was retarded when mixed with either FITZAP-4D or FITZAP-8D in vitro, albeit less dramatically than the ex vivo samples (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: In vivo interactions likely enable co-purification of lysin/sp18 and FITZAP from sperm lysate.
source: Together, these findings support that in vivo interactions likely enable co-purification of lysin/sp18 and FITZAP from sperm lysate.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the chromatography data.

claim: FITZAP-8D is an intrinsically disordered protein as revealed by chemical shift analysis.
source: Chemical shift analysis of FITZAP-8D revealed that it is an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP); even when bound to lysin, FITZAP-8D remained highly dynamic and adopted no regular secondary structure (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Even when bound to lysin, FITZAP-8D remained highly dynamic and adopted no regular secondary structure.
source: Chemical shift analysis of FITZAP-8D revealed that it is an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP); even when bound to lysin, FITZAP-8D remained highly dynamic and adopted no regular secondary structure (Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Lysin and FITZAP form a fuzzy complex that exists in an ensemble of different interchanging configurations.
source: Thus, lysin and FITZAP form a fuzzy complex: protein complexes that exist in an ensemble of different interchanging configurations (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and illustrated in Figure 2.

claim: Formation of the fuzzy complex is primarily due to packing between hydrophobic amino acids in residues 21–29 of FITZAP and an exposed hydrophobic face on lysin near the nexus of the N- and C-termini.
source: Formation of the fuzzy complex is primarily due to packing between hydrophobic amino acids in residues 21–29 of FITZAP (Figure 3A) and an exposed hydrophobic face on lysin near the nexus of the N- and C-termini.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 3A.

claim: Covering the hydrophobic patch of lysin with FITZAP imparts a high net negative charge to this region of lysin.
source: Covering this hydrophobic patch with FITZAP imparts a high net negative charge to this region of lysin, likely explaining the affinity of lysin to anion exchange resins when FITZAP is present.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the binding data.

claim: The FITZAP-binding region of lysin is the same surface that recognizes its egg receptor VERL.
source: Significantly, the FITZAP-binding region of lysin is also the same surface that recognizes its egg receptor VERL, based on both chemical shift perturbations (Figure 2A) and paramagnetic relaxation enhancement (PRE) data (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The exposed hydrophobic surface of lysin is likely why purified lysin has a much lower in vitro solubility limit compared to the acrosome where FITZAP is also highly abundant.
source: This exposed hydrophobic surface is likely why purified lysin has a much lower in vitro solubility limit compared to the acrosome where FITZAP is also highly abundant.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the structural data.

claim: Under both low-salt and high-salt conditions, the hydrophobic patch of FITZAP interacts with lysin.
source: Under both conditions, the hydrophobic patch of FITZAP interacts with lysin, yet NMR intensity perturbation of the poly-aspartate region was only observed under low-salt concentrations where intermolecular salt bridges may form (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 3B.

claim: NMR intensity perturbation of the poly-aspartate region was only observed under low-salt concentrations where intermolecular salt bridges may form.
source: Under both conditions, the hydrophobic patch of FITZAP interacts with lysin, yet NMR intensity perturbation of the poly-aspartate region was only observed under low-salt concentrations where intermolecular salt bridges may form (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 3B.

claim: Lysin and FITZAP undergo slower subunit exchange under low-salt concentrations.
source: Differences in NMR perturbation establish that lysin and FITZAP undergo slower subunit exchange under low-salt concentrations (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by NMR data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Equimolar mixtures of lysin and FITZAP-8D under low-salt conditions form extremely large oligomers with an average diameter of ~400 nm.
source: Equimolar mixtures of lysin and FITZAP-8D under low-salt conditions form extremely large oligomers with an average diameter of ~400 nm (compared to a mean lysin diameter of ~6 nm); these large particles are not present at high-salt concentrations (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by dynamic light scattering data in Figure 4.

claim: Large lysin-FITZAP particles are not present at high-salt concentrations.
source: Equimolar mixtures of lysin and FITZAP-8D under low-salt conditions form extremely large oligomers with an average diameter of ~400 nm (compared to a mean lysin diameter of ~6 nm); these large particles are not present at high-salt concentrations (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by dynamic light scattering data in Figure 4.

claim: Upon secretion into seawater, FITZ complexes are disrupted and subunit exchange rate increases, allowing lysin to be rapidly liberated from FITZAP.
source: Upon secretion into seawater, the FITZ complexes are disrupted and subunit exchange rate increases, allowing lysin to be rapidly liberated from FITZAP, permitting interactions with VERL via a common binding interface.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the salt-dependent binding data.

claim: The formation and dissolution of FITZ complexes based on environmental context provides a mechanism for exceptionally high packaging concentrations of lysin inside the sperm acrosome as well as its rapid dispersal in seawater.
source: The formation and dissolution of FITZ complexes based on the environmental context provides a mechanism for exceptionally high packaging concentrations of lysin inside the sperm acrosome as well as its rapid dispersal in seawater when fertilization may be imminent.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a summary of the functional significance of FITZ complexes.

claim: Lysin and VERL are rapidly coevolving sperm and egg proteins that exhibit species-specific interactions.
source: Lysin and VERL are rapidly coevolving sperm and egg proteins that exhibit species-specific interactions (Wilburn and Swanson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: Lysin had greater affinity for the high-D FITZAP isoforms compared to low-D forms.
source: Lysin had greater affinity for the high-D FITZAP isoforms compared to low-D forms.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5A.

claim: For all three species, lysin bound the conspecific high-D isoforms of FITZAP with equilibrium dissociation constants of ~1–2 μM under intracellular salt conditions.
source: For all three species, lysin bound the conspecific high-D isoforms of FITZAP with equilibrium dissociation constants of ~1–2 μM under intracellular salt conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5A.

claim: Except for disk lysin and red FITZAP-8D, all cases of heterospecific binding were significantly weaker, supporting lysin-FITZAP coevolution.
source: Except for disk lysin and red FITZAP-8D, all cases of heterospecific binding were significantly weaker, supporting lysin-FITZAP coevolution (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5A.

claim: Under seawater conditions, there was a ≥ 20 fold decrease in conspecific binding affinity.
source: Under seawater conditions, there was a ≥ 20 fold decrease in conspecific binding affinity (Figure 5B), consistent with the liberation of lysin from FITZ complexes after its release from the acrosome.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5B.

claim: Green sp18 shows tighter binding to conspecific FITZAP-4D compared to FITZAP-1D.
source: Green sp18 shows tighter binding to conspecific FITZAP-4D compared to FITZAP-1D; however, the relative affinity of sp18 for 4D over 1D (77/22 = 3.5 X) is greater than that of lysin (>100 X), suggesting that sp18 has higher preference for low D isoforms compared to lysin.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5C.

claim: The relative affinity of sp18 for 4D over 1D (77/22 = 3.5 X) is greater than that of lysin (>100 X), suggesting that sp18 has higher preference for low D isoforms compared to lysin.
source: Green sp18 shows tighter binding to conspecific FITZAP-4D compared to FITZAP-1D; however, the relative affinity of sp18 for 4D over 1D (77/22 = 3.5 X) is greater than that of lysin (>100 X), suggesting that sp18 has higher preference for low D isoforms compared to lysin.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by fluorescence polarization data in Figure 5C.

claim: Correlated rates of molecular evolution between sp18 and low-D FITZAP isoforms are consistent with coevolution.
source: We indeed observe correlated rates of molecular evolution between sp18 and low-D FITZAP isoforms, consistent with coevolution (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by evolutionary analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Both evolutionary and biochemical evidence support that FITZAP isoforms have subfunctionalized to respond to the divergent evolutionary trajectories of lysin and sp18.
source: Therefore, both evolutionary and biochemical evidence support that FITZAP isoforms have subfunctionalized to respond to the divergent evolutionary trajectories of lysin and sp18.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the binding and evolutionary data.

claim: VERL imposes direct sexual selection on lysin and indirect sexual selection on FITZAP.
source: We propose a system of tethered coevolution between VERL, lysin, and FITZAP where VERL imposes direct sexual selection on lysin and indirect sexual selection on FITZAP (summarized in Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as the main model proposed by the study.

claim: Lysin evolves ~5X faster than its coevolving regions of VERL.
source: Second, lysin evolves ~5X faster than its coevolving regions of VERL (Galindo et al., 2003), suggesting that it is experiencing greater directional selection than VERL.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: Lysin, but not VERL, is monomorphic within some abalone populations and experienced recent selective sweeps.
source: Lysin, but not VERL, is also monomorphic within some abalone populations and experienced recent selective sweeps (Clark et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: In sea urchins, longitudinal measurements of allele frequencies for gamete recognition proteins support that female proteins will shift to lower affinity interactions in response to increased polyspermy risk, and high-affinity binding is restored by adaptation of male proteins.
source: Third, in sea urchins (another organism with broadcast spawning), longitudinal measurements of allele frequencies for gamete recognition proteins support that female proteins will shift to lower affinity interactions in response to increased polyspermy risk, and high-affinity binding is restored by adaptation of male proteins (Levitan et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation to Levitan et al., 2019.

claim: Evolutionary dynamics of lysin are more responsive to VERL than vice versa.
source: This suggests that evolutionary dynamics of lysin are more responsive to VERL than vice versa.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the sea urchin data.

claim: FITZAP is an IDP whose function is to facilitate the storage and dispersal of fertilization proteins.
source: Fourth, as FITZAP is an IDP whose function is to facilitate the storage and dispersal of fertilization proteins, we anticipate reduced conservation on its primary sequence from intramolecular epistasis, with its evolution mostly being driven by directional selection imposed by its binding partners.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a characterization of FITZAP function.

claim: IDPs lack a single favored conformation and experience less purifying selection compared to structural domains.
source: Because IDPs lack a single favored conformation, they experience less purifying selection (or slower evolution relative to genetic drift) to maintain a tertiary fold and have lower sequence conservation (Brown et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: IDPs experience more positive selection compared to structural domains.
source: Beyond relaxed purifying selection and greater rates of genetic drift, IDPs also experience more positive selection compared to structural domains (Afanasyeva et al., 2018), presumably in response to coevolution with their binding partners.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: FITZAP is expected to respond more to selection from lysin than vice versa.
source: We expect FITZAP to respond more to selection from lysin than vice versa.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an expectation based on FITZAP being an IDP.

claim: Intrinsic disorder may be a mechanism of adaptation to shifts in environmental conditions.
source: It has been suggested that intrinsic disorder may be a mechanism of adaptation to shifts in environmental conditions; for example, host-changing parasites have higher genome-wide levels of predicted protein disorder compared to obligate intracellular parasites and endosymbiotes (Pancsa and Tompa, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citation.

claim: The change in ionic strength experienced by secreted proteins of most marine animals is likely an extreme example of shifts between chemical environments.
source: The change in ionic strength experienced by secreted proteins of most marine animals is likely an extreme example of such shifts between chemical environments.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the environmental context.

claim: The intrinsic disorder of FITZAP may be crucial to its apparent structural versatility and high evolvability in response to a rapidly coevolving partner.
source: The intrinsic disorder of FITZAP may be crucial to its apparent structural versatility and high evolvability in response to a rapidly coevolving partner.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of FITZAP's properties.

claim: Across animals, plants, and microbes, genes associated with fertilization usually evolve faster than the rest of the genome.
source: Across animals, plants, and microbes, genes associated with fertilization usually evolve faster than the rest of the genome (Swanson and Vacquier, 2002; Wilburn et al., 2017; Wilburn and Swanson, 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and supported by citations.

claim: Direct sexual selection can drive elaboration of molecular phenotypes such as the extraordinary abundance of lysin and sp18.
source: Like macroscopic secondary sex characters, direct sexual selection can drive elaboration of molecular phenotypes such as the extraordinary abundance of lysin and sp18.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Sequence differences that yield species-specific interactions with coevolving receptors are one of many reproductive barriers that likely contribute to speciation.
source: Combined with sequence differences that yield species-specific interactions with coevolving receptors, these proteins are one of many reproductive barriers that likely contribute to speciation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the evolutionary significance.

claim: Indirect selection may propagate throughout the sperm proteome and be a general mechanism to explain accelerated gametic protein evolution.
source: Indirect selection may further propagate throughout the sperm proteome and be a general mechanism to explain accelerated gametic protein evolution.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a broader implication of the findings.

claim: The intracellular environment of marine animals is less concentrated in salt than seawater.
source: The total salt concentration of seawater is ~500 mM, yet the intracellular environment of marine animals is less concentrated.
evidence: This is stated in the results as background information.

claim: Many invertebrates such as abalone are osmoconformers and use high intracellular concentrations of free amino acids, betaines, and other highly soluble metabolites to achieve osmolality.
source: Osmolality is maintained in marine vertebrates by active transport of water and ions, whereas many invertebrates such as abalone are osmoconformers and use high intracellular concentrations of free amino acids, betaines, and other highly soluble metabolites to achieve osmolality (but not isotonicity) (Venter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: The exact intracellular concentration of inorganic ions in abalone sperm is unknown but likely much lower than seawater based on data from sea urchin gametes and other abalone tissues.
source: While the exact intracellular concentration of inorganic ions in abalone sperm is unknown, it is likely much lower than seawater based on data from sea urchin gametes (Horthschild and Barnes, 1953; Rodríguez and Darszon, 2003) and other abalone tissues (Jia and Liu, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations to related organisms.

claim: The inorganic salt concentration may be even lower in the acrosome where the acrosomal proteins may themselves serve as osmolytes.
source: The inorganic salt concentration may be even lower in the acrosome where the acrosomal proteins – given their extraordinary concentrations and net charges – may themselves serve as osmolytes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a speculation about the acrosomal environment.

claim: Lysin and sp18 are paralogs with similar tertiary structures that have subfunctionalized following gene duplication.
source: Lysin and sp18 are paralogs with similar tertiary structures that have subfunctionalized following gene duplication (Kresge et al., 2001; Swanson and Vacquier, 1995), so the multiple FITZAP isoforms may also have subfunctionalized to bind these different paralogs.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citations.

claim: The multiple FITZAP isoforms may have subfunctionalized to bind lysin and sp18 paralogs.
source: Lysin and sp18 are paralogs with similar tertiary structures that have subfunctionalized following gene duplication (Kresge et al., 2001; Swanson and Vacquier, 1995), so the multiple FITZAP isoforms may also have subfunctionalized to bind these different paralogs.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a hypothesis.

claim: Tighter co-elution between lysin/FITZAP-8D and sp18/FITZAP-4D was observed in red abalone anion exchange experiments.
source: For our anion exchange experiments in red abalone, we observed tighter co-elution between lysin/FITZAP-8D and sp18/FITZAP-4D (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1.

claim: Male abalone have overlapping habitat ranges and spawning periods such that there is opportunity for hybridization to occur.
source: Male abalone have overlapping habitat ranges and spawning periods such that there is opportunity for hybridization to occur.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption as context for the model.

claim: Sperm are attracted to eggs via chemotaxis.
source: Sperm are attracted to eggs via chemotaxis and bind to the vitelline envelope (A).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption as part of the fertilization process.

claim: At the stage when sperm bind to the vitelline envelope, the acrosome is still intact with lysin and FITZAP tightly packaged as FITZ complexes.
source: At this stage, the acrosome is still intact (Lewis et al., 1982) with lysin and FITZAP tightly packaged as FITZ complexes.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption and supported by citation.

claim: Binding to the VE causes the sperm to acrosome react.
source: Binding to the VE causes the sperm to acrosome react (B), releasing its contents into highly ionic seawater which disperses lysin and FITZAP.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption as part of the fertilization process.

claim: Liberated lysin can dissolve the VE by binding VERL domains.
source: Liberated lysin can now dissolve the VE by binding VERL domains (C); these interactions are species-specific and provide one barrier to hybridization (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption and supported by citation.

claim: Lysin-VERL interactions are species-specific and provide one barrier to hybridization.
source: Liberated lysin can now dissolve the VE by binding VERL domains (C); these interactions are species-specific and provide one barrier to hybridization (Swanson and Vacquier, 1997).
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption and supported by citation.

claim: The rapid evolution of lysin is driven by direct sexual selection to maintain sperm-egg interactions.
source: Because the rapid evolution of lysin is driven by direct sexual selection to maintain sperm-egg interactions, and FITZAP is co-evolving to bind the same interface, VERL imposes indirect sexual selection onto FITZAP.
evidence: This is stated in Figure 6 caption as part of the model.

claim: Different species of abalone express different numbers of FITZAP isoforms named for the length of the N-terminal poly-aspartate region.
source: Different species of abalone express different numbers of FITZAP isoforms named for the length of the N-terminal poly-aspartate region (Palmer, 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by citation.

claim: Green abalone has two FITZAP isoforms with shorter poly-aspartate regions (1D and 4D).
source: Like red abalone, green abalone has two FITZAP isoforms but with shorter poly-aspartate regions (1D and 4D), while disk abalone has a single FITZAP isoform with an even longer poly-aspartate array (11D).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a characterization of FITZAP isoforms across species.

claim: Disk abalone has a single FITZAP isoform with an even longer poly-aspartate array (11D).
source: Like red abalone, green abalone has two FITZAP isoforms but with shorter poly-aspartate regions (1D and 4D), while disk abalone has a single FITZAP isoform with an even longer poly-aspartate array (11D).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a characterization of FITZAP isoforms across species.

claim: The specificity of disk FITZAP-11D to disk lysin supports that electrostatic attraction alone is not sufficient to explain FITZ complex formation.
source: Both hydrophobic and ionic interactions likely contribute to these higher affinity complexes, yet the specificity of disk FITZAP-11D (with the longest poly-aspartate array) to disk lysin supports that electrostatic attraction alone is not sufficient to explain FITZ complex formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the binding data.

claim: Both hydrophobic and ionic interactions likely contribute to higher affinity lysin-FITZAP complexes.
source: Both hydrophobic and ionic interactions likely contribute to these higher affinity complexes, yet the specificity of disk FITZAP-11D (with the longest poly-aspartate array) to disk lysin supports that electrostatic attraction alone is not sufficient to explain FITZ complex formation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the binding data.
